title: Razorfen Downs
body: Razorfen Downs lies deep in the Razorfen at the southern edge of the Barrens, entered through the great maw that the quilboar hold to be their boar god's own. It was long the chief city of the quilboar. Now it belongs to the dead. Withered quilboar, risen from their own kind, guard its bramble halls beside withered battle boars, and further in, skeletons, ghouls and spirits of the bitter cold crowd the winding paths. The living who fight beside them are of the Death's Head: geomancers who hurl fire, and necromancers armored in bone who wield shadow. Near the entrance, fires burn at a great idol. Deepest of all, on a height above the lowest reaches, the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer keeps his seat, and the air grows colder the nearer one comes to him. Champions come here from Stormwind and from the Undercity, and others come for the living the quilboar drag in from the plains.

parts.body: Ragglesnout does not always stand in the Downs, but when he is there he is hard to miss: a quilboar of great size who fights with shadow. He hurled bolts of darkness, laid a word of pain on his foes that gnawed at them, and seized a foe's mind to turn it against its friends, and he had healing magic as well. None of it saved him. He fell among the thorns.

title: The Holding Pens
body: Far from the entrance, past the idol and the hall of the gong, the quilboar of the Downs keep pens for the living. They stand at the far end of the Downs, walled in by bramble, with withered quilboar walking the paths nearby. Few would expect to find anyone still alive in this place, but the pens are not empty. Two men are held in them, and with them an ogre, Sah'rhee. What the quilboar mean to do with the people they carry off from the Barrens, nothing in the pens says.

parts.body: One of the two men is Henry Stern, a cook and an alchemist from Stormwind. He came to the Barrens looking for local herbs and recipes for his uncle Angus, and the quilboar caught him. He thanks whoever freed him with all his heart. If no one had come along, he says, he is sure he would have ended up in their stew pot.

title: The Gong
body: Between the idol near the entrance and the pens at the far end of the Downs, a broad hall opens in the bramble. Necromancers of the Death's Head stand there among withered reavers and quilguards, and dark corridors lead off from it into the thorns. At the side of the hall hangs a great gong. No one standing there can say what it is for.

parts.body: The gong was answered. At its first sounding tomb fiends, small crypt fiends, poured out of the corridors and threw themselves at whoever stood near. When they were dead it rang again, and larger tomb reavers came, binding their foes in webs. At the third sounding Tuten'kash crawled out of the dark, a crypt fiend of monstrous size. Its curse dragged at every spell and blow around it and its webs pinned all before it, but it died in the hall, and the gong fell silent.

title: Amnennar the Coldbringer
body: Amnennar the Coldbringer is a lich, and he keeps his seat on a height deep within Razorfen Downs, above the lowest reaches where the dead crowd thickest. A shell of frost clings about him, and spirits of the bitter cold drift through the halls on the way up to him. Anyone who would reach him must first pass the great abomination that lumbers through the depths at the foot of his height.

parts.body: The Downs did not always seem so dark. Once it looked like the home of simple quilboar and little threat to anyone, but what has been found there since is far more serious. The quilboar of the Downs have made a pact with the Scourge, and the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer rules them now.
sources: quest 3636 description (once the home of simple quilboar; a pact was made with the Scourge, creating creatures far worse; now ruled by the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer)
quest 3341 description (first observations revealed little threat; the quilboar of Razorfen Downs have aligned themselves with the Scourge; a lich named Amnennar rules them now)

parts.body: To any who have heard Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar, this may be the answer he sought. He feared that treachery lay behind the corruption of the resting place of Agamaggan, long held to be pure, and here the boar god's own people have struck a bargain with the Scourge.
sources: quest 3636 description (a pact was made with the Scourge); quest 1101 reward text (Falfindel hopes to learn what corrupted the resting place of Agamaggan and fears the answer lies in treachery; AllowableRaces 1101, Alliance only)
feralas.json 35725 part 2 and 35731 part 2, pointed to in one phrase; the link between the corruption and the pact is offered as a possibility, since no quest text makes it

parts.body: In the Undercity, Andrew Brownell of the Magic Quarter says more. The lich controls the quilboar's every move by the power of his vast mind, and he holds a direct link of thought to Ner'zhul himself. That bond must be severed, Brownell says, and an end must come to the Coldbringer.
sources: quest 3341 description (using the power of his massive consciousness to control their every move; a direct telepathic link to Ner'zhul; we must sever this bond; an end must come to the Coldbringer) and QuestCompletionLog (Andrew Brownell at the Magic Quarter in the Undercity); AllowableRaces 690

parts.body: Amnennar met intruders with a promise that they would never leave this place alive. He struck with frost, freezing foes where they stood and hurling them back from him. As his wounds mounted he named himself the hand of the Lich King and drew wraiths out of the freezing air, calling on his servants and the spirits to attend their master. The Coldbringer fell on his height all the same.
sources: creature_text 7358 groups 0 (You'll never leave this place alive), 3 (I am the hand of the Lich King), 5 (begins to summon wraiths out of the freezing cold air), 1 (To me, my servants) and 2 (Come, spirits - attend your master)

parts.body: In the Cathedral of Light, Archbishop Benedictus gave his thanks. The Scourge, he said, will now think twice before it tries to bolster its ranks again, and he blessed in the name of the Light the one who had ended the lich.

parts.body: Andrew Brownell had made plain what was at stake: any attempt by the Scourge to bolster its ranks had to be stopped. When the lich's skull was laid before him, he was satisfied. The loyalty of a lich is unswerving, he said; let the Scourge learn that such loyalty brings them only destruction.

title: Belnistrasz
body: Belnistrasz is a prisoner of the quilboar, held in their pens deep in Razorfen Downs, who had given himself up for dead, or worse, for a meal for the vermin around him. Freed, he names the danger plainly. The Scourge have brokered some sort of deal with the quilboar here, he says, and this nightmare is the result. Rather than simply flee, he means to make a difference for everyone's sake, and he asks his rescuers to help him, though it will be dangerous. He gives them an oathstone, to be handed back to him if they agree to help.

parts.body: Belnistrasz cares nothing for politics, he says. Whether his helpers are of the Horde or the Alliance means nothing to him: what matters is stamping out direct and dire threats to all the races, and there is a large one here. He is not from these parts, he admits, and among his kind an oathstone is a bond of agreement. When it came back to him he was delighted, and set about telling his new allies what has been going on.
sources: quest 3523 request text (not one for politics; Horde or Alliance; squelching direct and dire threats to all the races, and a large one in here; not from around these parts; an oathstone important to people of my kind as a bond of agreement) and reward text (I thought you looked to be the heroic type; let me bring you up to speed)

parts.body: In the brazier Belnistrasz left behind, a vision waited. Those who gazed into its flame saw a great-winged red dragon fill their minds, and heard Belnistrasz's voice, rougher now, speaking to them directly. They were the heroes he had hoped for, he said. The butchery the quilboar had worked here was a thing of the past, and his faith in mortals had been renewed once more.
sources: quest 3525 reward text (Belnistrasz's sudden departure has left a burning brazier; the image of a great-winged red dragon fills your mind; a more graveled version of Belnistrasz's voice; the heroes I had hoped you would be; the butchery a thing of the past; my faith in mortals renewed)

title: Mordresh Fire Eye
body: Mordresh Fire Eye is a towering skeleton, twice the size of a common one, who keeps to the far reaches of the Downs, not far from the pens where the quilboar hold their captives. He is no mindless thing of bone. He has a voice of his own, and a name that speaks of fire in a place where the dead mostly bring the cold.

parts.body: Those who came near him heard his boasts: the Scourge would enslave the quilboar, spread across this barren land and soon rule the world. He spoke of the quilboar as slaves to be taken, not as allies. He met intruders with a cry to his brethren to slay them for the Scourge, and the dead nearby came at his call. He answered with fire, hurling it and loosing bursts of flame on any who came close, but he fell all the same.

title: Glutton
body: Glutton is a hulking abomination stitched together from dead flesh, larger than any of the ghouls around it. It lumbers through the lowest reaches of the Downs, at the foot of the height where the lich keeps his seat, and anyone climbing toward Amnennar must pass its way. A cloud of disease hangs about it at all times, a reek of rot that sickens anyone who comes too near.

parts.body: Glutton bellowed as it struck that it smelled the stench of the living. As the fight wore on it grew hungry, then very hungry, and fell into a frenzy, lashing out faster and harder in its need to feed. It never fed. The abomination collapsed in the depths of the Downs, below the lich's height.

title: Extinguishing the Idol
body: Near the entrance of Razorfen Downs stands an idol, and Belnistrasz has learned what it is for. It is an oven, a macabre one: in it the quilboar consume the captives they carry off from the Barrens. He can shut the idol down and bind the quilboar from ever using it again, by a ritual, but not alone. He asks to be escorted to the idol and guarded once he begins, for while the ritual holds him he will barely be able to speak, let alone defend himself. If the quilboar bring him down, he warns, it is all over.

parts.body: The quilboar did not let the ritual go unchallenged. Last of all those sent against it came Plaguemaw the Rotting, a great quilboar rotting on his feet. His stench hung over the idol, sapping the strength and quickness of all who breathed it and choking off their spells. He fell beside the idol all the same.
sources: creature 7356 Plaguemaw the Rotting: no spawn; summoned by npc_idol_room_spawner when its data is 7, the eighth and last spawner of the ritual, about four minutes in; data 7 summons him alone, without boars or geomancers (razorfen_downs.cpp); display 6124, QuillBoar model at scale 1.5; type 7

parts.body: Belnistrasz led the way from the pens to the idol, warning his escort to stay close, for the fiends here leap out of the shadows. At the idol he began: the ritual would take about five minutes. The Downs answered with wave after wave of withered battle boars, Death's Head geomancers and withered quilguards, while he called out the minutes as the power built. Then it was done. The idol's fires went out for good, and Belnistrasz was gone, leaving a burning brazier behind.

title: An Unholy Alliance
body: On the body of Charlga Razorflank, the crone of Razorfen Kraul, lies a small scroll. It is a letter, addressed to My Lady and signed by Ambassador Malcin. He reminds her of what he has offered: the chance to take the Barrens and the lands beyond. In return he asks only her aid, by which he means the freedom to act in the area. He would talk further, for they have great power and will share it with those wise enough to join them. For now, he writes, he will remain outside Razorfen Downs. The scroll is to be carried to the Royal Quarter of the Undercity.

parts.body: In the Royal Quarter, Varimathras knew the insignia on the scroll. Malcin, he said, was one of the Scourge's plagued servants, once a human diplomat to the kingdom of Lordaeron, before things changed. It seems the Scourge are not content with one continent, and if they are trying to gain a foothold in Kalimdor, it falls to the Undercity to act.
sources: quest 6522 reward text (I recognize the insignia; found on the crone who reigns over Razorfen Kraul; the Scourge aren't content with one continent; Ambassador Malcin one of the Scourge's plagued servants, a human diplomat to the kingdom of Lordaeron before things changed; up to us to act)

creature_questender 2425 Varimathras for 6522 (base data); mod-individual-progression zone_undercity.sql spawns Varimathras (guid 602425) in the Royal Quarter in phase IPP_PHASE_II (before the Battle for the Undercity, IndividualProgression.cpp AREA_UNDERCITY) and removes 6522 from disables

parts.body: Malcin must be slain, Varimathras decided, and his mission made a failure in the eyes of the Lich King. His presence explains much of what the Forsaken have found around the Downs. Some of the quilboar there have grown frightfully powerful, while showing signs of the Plague in their own way: surely the mark of some deal they have struck.
sources: quest 6521 description (this ambassador must be slain, his mission a failure in the eyes of the Lich King; some of the quilboar have grown frightfully powerful while showing signs of the Plague in their own way; a sign of some sort of deal they have struck); AllowableRaces 690, QuestType 2, flags 8, PrevQuestID 6522
creature_queststarter 2425 for 6521 (base data); reachable only with mod-individual-progression (disables removed in zone_undercity.sql)

parts.body: Malcin was found where he had said he would be, outside Razorfen Downs, and slain, and his head was carried to the Undercity. The Scourge must not take a foothold on Kalimdor, Varimathras said. The one hopeful sign was the crone: she seemed uncorrupted, as if she knew in her spirit that the Barrens would never truly be hers if she took the Scourge's deal. With Malcin dead the Scourge's advance was halted, and the Dark Lady sent her thanks. How far their influence reaches within the Downs, no one yet knows.
sources: quest 6521 log text (bring Ambassador Malcin's Head), request text (we cannot afford to allow the Scourge to take a foothold on Kalimdor; the crone seemed uncorrupted; the Barrens would not truly be hers if she were to agree to their deal) and reward text (now that Malcin is dead the Scourge's advances will be halted; the Dark Lady thanks you; we do not know the extent of the Scourge's influence within the Downs)

parts.body: In the Royal Quarter, Bragor Bloodfist knew the insignia on the scroll from his time in Northrend, and he had no doubts. Malcin is plainly one of the Lich King's servants, and that makes him a target. Bragor will not let the Scourge get a foothold here: they are not going to take Kalimdor.
sources: quest 14352 reward text (I've seen the insignia on this scroll before during my time in Northrend; this Malcin is one of the Lich King's servants, and that makes him a target; they're not going to take Kalimdor); creature_questender 36273 Bragor Bloodfist
undercity.json 149706 (Bragor, requiredState 13), named only

parts.body: Bragor's contacts in Orgrimmar had sent word that their scouts found signs of the Plague around the Downs, and quilboar showing it too, and far more powerful for it. Malcin was found outside Razorfen Downs and slain, and his head went to Bragor. It was a deed that did the Horde proud, he said, keeping the Scourge from setting down roots on its soil. What they have done in the Downs is not yet known, but it will be: they cannot slink around in the dark forever.
sources: quest 14353 description (my contacts in Orgrimmar tell me their scouts have found signs of the Plague down there; the quilboar are showing signs of being plagued too, much more powerful; find this Malcin and kill him), log text (bring Ambassador Malcin's Head) and reward text (you've done the Horde proud by stopping the Scourge from setting down roots on our soil; we may not know everything they've done in the Downs, but we'll find out; they can't slink around in the dark forever)

notes: Check: the module claims verified in zone_undercity.sql: Charlga's 49205 replaced by 17008 (same Horde condition), disables on 6521 and 6522 deleted, Varimathras 2425 spawned (guid 602425, phaseMask IPPPHASE_II) and IndividualProgression.cpp AREA_UNDERCITY gives phase II until 13267 (or the Alliance battle) is rewarded, phase III after; Bragor 31901 is phase III only. The module also makes Varimathras an ender of 14352 and 14353 and points their texts at him, but with 49205 gone nothing starts 14352. (b) module before 13 and (c) module at 13 or later before the battle: opening on ACCEPT 6522, parts 1-3 with Varimathras present; parts 4-5 unearnable (minState 13 kept as a guard). (d) module after the battle: the scroll still starts 6522 but its ender Varimathras is phased out and Bragor ends neither 6522 nor 6521, so only the opening can be earned; it holds. Parts 1-3 stay untagged: no state marks the battle, and a maxState would hide them from (c). Part 1: 'for the Forsaken' made 'the Undercity' (the text says us). Two versions of one chain: without the module, Charlga's scroll starts 14352 (ended by Bragor Bloodfist 36273) and Bragor gives 14353; with mod-individual-progression (zone_undercity.sql) the scroll is 17008 and starts 6522, the classic quests 6521/6522 are taken out of disables, and Varimathras 2425 stands in the Royal Quarter in IPP phase II (every character before the Battle for the Undercity), starting 6521 and ending 6522 and 6521. title: A Host of Evil
body: Outside the maw of Razorfen Downs, the night elf Myriam Moonsinger keeps her watch on the undead diplomat there, and she has drawn her own conclusion. The Forsaken, as far as she has seen, do not pass on their illness to others, and so she has begun to think this one is of the Scourge. For now he is not her concern. The growing ranks around him are: Razorfen battleguards and thornweavers, and cultists of the Death's Head, who creep from the shadows every day. She is not strong enough to fight them alone, and she asks for help in hunting them.

parts.body: The hunt left Myriam in no doubt. Seeing even this small sample of the diplomat's power, she says, has removed any doubt she had that the Scourge are one of the greatest threats this world has ever seen. She will go on studying him and the quilboar around him. For those who want a greater challenge she points to the cave nearby, shaped like the maw of a great boar: inside, she is sure, they will find one.
sources: quest 6626 request text (seeing this small sample of the diplomat's power removes any doubt that the Scourge are one of the greatest threats this world has ever seen) and reward text (I will continue my study of this diplomat and the rest of the quilboar; head into the cave that looks like a great boar maw; greater challenges inside)
